The Official Comment to§ 1-203 is amended by adding the following 
language at the end of the first paragraph: 
This section does not support an independent cause of 
action for failure to perform or enforce in good faith. Rather, this 
section means that a failure to perform or enforce, in good faith, 
a specific duty or obligation under the contract, constitutes a 
breach of that contract 
or makes unavailable, 
under the 
particular 
circumstances, 
a remedial right or power. This 
distinction makes it clear that the doctrine of good faith merely 
directs a court towards 
interpreting 
contracts 
within the 
commercial context in which they are created, performed, and 
enforced, and does not create a separate dut, of fairness and 
reasonableness which can be independently breached.
